newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets price for sorghum in Tamaulipas state.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets price for sorghum in Tamaulipas state.

text.p: Mexico has set prices for sorghum in the northeastern state of Tamaulipas at 900 pesos per tonne starting this week, the Agriculture Ministry said Monday in a statement.

Following a visit to Tamaulipas by Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa, the ministry said the price, pacted between sorghum growers and livestock farmers, was set to avoid sorghum sales grinding to a halt in wars over price.

Labastida added a federal fund of 400 million pesos had also been created to subsidize sorghum sales this crop cycle in the country's top sorghum growing zone. If prices dipped below 900 pesos per tonne, farmers would receive subsidies upto the agreed price, he said,
Tamaulipas farmers expect a crop this year of 1.5-1.8 million tonnes. The Agriculture Ministry expects a crop around 2 million tonnes from the state.

Tamaulipas state Gov. Manuel Cavazos Lerma said the state was contemplating, as an additional measure to help farmers, handing over the adminstration and operation of state-owned warehouses to store and sell sorghum.

Cavazos Lerma, cited in the same statement, said Tamaulipas was also considering financial supports to encourage sorghum planting on irrigated lands in the northern part of the state. A new reservoir to boost irrigated plantings was also under study, he added.
